subject: Pilot top-up: hybrid credit + time extension proposal
messages:
From: Ellie Park <ellie@astralabs.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-24T14:15:00-08:00
Subject: Pilot top-up options — quick clarification

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the demo and for supporting our pilot. We’re seeing promising results but have burned faster than expected during model tuning. Can you confirm whether Redwood prefers to do: (A) a short time extension (additional 14 days) at the current rate, or (B) an upfront top-up of credits (prepaid token/compute credits) that we can consume immediately?

Two asks: 1) rough cost delta between A and B, and 2) whether you can provide a mixed option (small duration extension + smaller credit top-up). Procurement will want an invoice/PO flow if we go with credits.

Appreciate a quick read — we’re trying to pick by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Ellie Park
Director of ML Engineering
AstraLabs
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: Ellie Park <ellie@astralabs.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-24T16:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pilot top-up options — quick clarification

Hi Ellie —

Great to hear the pilot is producing signal. Short answer: we can do either; the unit economics and legal flow differ. High-level options: 

1) Time extension (14 days) — no upfront invoice required, keep current trial terms. Best if you need runway for troubleshooting or more evaluation without procurement involvement.

2) Credit top-up (prepaid) — we issue an invoice/PO, credits apply immediately, and there’s a modest volume discount compared to on-demand. Credits give you capacity control and simpler long-term conversion bookkeeping.

3) Hybrid (what you suggested) — e.g., 7 extra days + a small 20k-credit top-up. This is our recommended path if you want immediate capacity and a soft runway.

I attached a short pricing summary and a one-page SOW draft that maps to each option. If you want, I can loop finance/legal to confirm invoicing and any PO requirements.

Link to HubSpot record: https://hubspot.company/contacts/ASTRA-3472

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-25T09:07:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: AstraLabs — pricing framing for top-up vs extension

Team — quick internal note so we present a crisp option set to Astra: 

Context: Astra is mid-pilot, burn > forecast due to larger eval prompts. They asked for either a pure extension, a credit top-up, or a hybrid. Procurement will likely want a PO if we go with credits.

Proposal (numbers are illustrative — will confirm with Soojin):
- Pure extension (14 days): no charge, but locks us into limited runway; use only if we want frictionless short-term goodwill.
- Credit top-up: $12k for 20k credits (roughly 40% markdown vs pay-as-you-go over short horizon). Requires PO/invoice, show as prepaid credit on their account.
- Hybrid: 7 day extension + $6k for 10k credits; gives immediate capacity and keeps procurement overhead down.

Risks: credits require finance to accept small PO. If procurement insists on net-45 + bigger value, we should push for a signed SOW and a modest discount to protect margin.

Ask: Marcus — ok to offer the hybrid? Karthik — any legal flags on short SOW addendum or invoice wording? Soojin — can you confirm billing flow and how quickly we can issue an invoice for $6k?

Thanks,
Jasmine
